title: Saving Venice from its own success
text: Venice {{1}} always been a city living on borrowed ground, its palaces resting on wooden piles driven {{2}} the mud of a shallow lagoon. Now the pressure on that ground is human: the historic centre has shrunk {{3}} more than 170,000 residents {{4}} under 50,000, {{5}} a result of soaring rents and the departure of ordinary jobs. Family homes are let {{6}} as holiday flats, bakeries become mask shops, and older Venetians describe 2020, {{7}} the crowds vanished overnight, as the quietest and strangest year of their lives. Entry fees, cruise-ship bans and resident-priority schemes are all being tried, {{8}} it remains to be seen whether any of them can restore the balance between a city and its own admirers.

gaps.explanation: Present perfect with a singular subject: has always been.
'Shrunk from X to Y' — the starting point takes 'from'.
The end point of the fall takes 'to'.

gaps.hint: preposition: ___ a result of soaring rents
gaps.explanation: 'As a result of' is the fixed phrase.

gaps.hint: particle: homes are let ___ as flats
gaps.explanation: 'Let out' — the particle shows renting to others.

gaps.hint: time relative: in 2020, ___ the crowds vanished
gaps.explanation: Non-defining time clause after the year.

gaps.hint: conjunction: schemes are tried, ___ it remains to be seen
gaps.explanation: The two clauses are simply added: and.
